title: Python SDK streaming protocol evolution and safe transform hooks
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Context: As the Redwood streaming chat event wire format evolves (structured deltas, new meta headers, and optional typed payloads), integrators using the Python SDK need a clear, low-risk path for handling protocol changes. This ticket implements a compatibility layer and developer-facing transform hook system that makes it safe to evolve event schemas without forcing immediate consumer upgrades.

Problem: Consumers today assume a flat set of event fields and do ad-hoc parsing. When new fields are introduced or event envelopes change, clients either crash on unexpected tokens or silently ignore important metadata. We need an explicit contract: stable headers, optional typed payloads, graceful fallback for unknown versions, and a discoverable adapter registry so SDK consumers can opt in to transformations (e.g., older apps transforming v2->v1 shape).

Goals:
- Provide a wire-version header in every event and a deterministic version negotiation strategy.
- Expose a lightweight plugin API (TransformHook) for per-connection or global adapters that can map unknown event shapes into a consumer-friendly structure.
- Ensure streaming iteration and backpressure semantics remain unchanged; hooks must not block the serving runtime.
- Emit targeted telemetry when adapters are invoked, or when unknown versions are dropped, to inform runtime/model teams.
- Ship examples and migration cookbook for application authors.
acceptance_criteria: Event objects delivered by the Python streaming iterator must include a 'wire_version' string header when present; SDK must default to '1' if missing.
Provide a TransformHook interface with two implementations: a no-op passthrough and a v2->v1 compatibility adapter used in the example app.
Hooks can be registered per-client and globally; registration API documented and covered by unit tests.
Unknown version handling path emits a telemetry counter ('stream.unknown_version') with the observed version and connection metadata.

End-to-end example demonstrating upgrading a client: running with the v2 wire format and a local adapter produces the same application-level messages as the legacy client (example code in examples/compat_adapter.py).
Bench: median per-event processing overhead for no-op hook is < 0.2ms on CI runner; hook invocation must not change streaming backpressure behavior in integration tests.
decision_log: 2026-03-10: Chose header-based wire_version vs. in-body version field to avoid repeated schema penalties and keep binary-friendly transports simple.

2026-03-11: TransformHook API will accept raw EventEnvelope + Context and return a sanitized EventEnvelope or raise TransformError. Raising signals consumer-level failure and increments telemetry; swallowing is possible but discouraged.

2026-03-12: Telemetry will be minimal: counters for adapter_invoked, adapter_error, unknown_version_seen, and histogram for transform_latency_ms. Rational: ops teams want signal without high cardinality.
2026-03-13: Decided against automatic remote-model-side translation because that creates coupling and increases latency; prefer local adapters and clear migration docs.
implementation_notes:
Implementation sketch: Add EventEnvelope.wire_version: str on the Python SDK event model (default '1'). Implement hooks module: class TransformHook(Protocol) with apply(envelope, ctx) -> envelope. Registry: Client(transform_hooks=[...]) and global register_transform_hook(hook, filter_predicate=None). Invocation: inside streaming iterator loop, call hook.apply in a small threadpool/executor if hook.is_async==True or inline if sync; but keep inline the default passthrough to avoid thread overhead. Use time.monotonic() to record latency and emit telemetry via telemetry.increment('stream.adapter_invoked') and telemetry.histogram('stream.transform_latency_ms', latency_ms).

Error handling: TransformError subclasses and context-rich messages. On TransformError: emit telemetry and surface to consumer by re-raising if adapter marked strict, otherwise emit warning log and drop event with telemetry increment('stream.adapter_dropped').

Compatibility adapter example: v2->v1 shim will map {header:{wv:'2',role:'assistant'}, payload:{content_blocks:[{type:'text',body:'...'}]}} -> {role:'assistant', delta:'...'} preserving timestamps and id mapping. Include helpers in sdk.utils: flatten_payload_blocks, safe_get, schema_assert.

Retries/interplay: Hooks must be idempotent since consumer may reprocess events on connection resume. Ensure adapter deterministic mapping and avoid mutating input envelope in place; always return new envelope object. Document behavior when adapters introduce new transient failures with guidance to set strict=True only when necessary.
test_plan:
Unit tests: hook registry registration/unregistration, no-op throughput microbench (assert <0.2ms), strict vs permissive adapter error paths.
Integration tests: local harness that spins up a synthetic streaming server emitting v1 and v2 envelopes and validates client's iterator yields normalized events under three modes: no hook (drop/raise), permissive hook (continues), strict hook (raises).
Fuzz tests: generate unknown wire_version strings and random payload shapes to ensure adapter errors are recorded but do not crash other client connections.
Load test: run streaming client with no-op hooks under 1k concurrent connections on CI perf pool and assert no regression in backpressure and average event latency.
Test artifacts: include example fixtures in tests/fixtures/{v1_sample.json,v2_sample.json,unknown_sample.json}.
rollout_plan:
- Phase 1 (canary): publish SDK alpha with TransformHook API and no-op default. Ship example adapters and ask 3 internal teams to opt-in. Monitor telemetry counters for unknown_version_seen and adapter_invoked.
- Phase 2 (wider): after 2 weeks and no regressions, promote to beta and add more adapters to examples. Update release notes and migration guide.
- Phase 3 (stable): include in sdk-python-2.7.0, mark API stable for one cycle. Provide migration checklist and deprecation warnings for code that relied on silent ignoring of unknown fields.
- Rollback: if adapter-induced errors exceed threshold (>=5% of streams erroring for 48h), publish patch disabling global adapters by default and notify teams.
